items.title: CVE-2026-0322 PAN-OS: Authenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) in the Management Interface (Severity: HIGH)
items.one_liner: Authenticated RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-0322) affecting Palo Alto PAN-OS management interfaces is seeing limited exploitation.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has disclosed CVE-2026-0322, an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the management interface of PAN-OS software impacting PA-Series, VM-Series, and Panorama devices. An authenticated attacker with network access can execute arbitrary code with root privileges, though exposure is significantly mitigated by restricting management access to trusted internal IP addresses. Limited active exploitation has been observed in the wild. While no direct workarounds exist, customers with Threat Prevention subscriptions can obtain limited coverage using specific Threat IDs tied to content versions 9159-10287 and later.
items.bottom_line: PAN-OS firewalls are exposed to authenticated root RCE via the management interface, requiring immediate restriction of management access.

items.title: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.4.2, 19.3.5, 19.2.8
items.one_liner: Immediate upgrade required for self-managed GitLab instances to patch a slew of critical and high-severity CVEs including Duo Agent Platform bypasses.
items.summary: GitLab released urgent patch versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8 to address multiple high and critical severity vulnerabilities affecting Community and Enterprise editions. The vulnerabilities include an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular expression compiler, improper authorization in downstream pipelines, and an input neutralization flaw within the GitLab Duo Agent Platform. Self-managed instances are strongly urged to upgrade immediately, as cloud environments and dedicated tenants have already been patched by the vendor. The security disclosures also cover various cross-site scripting, open redirect, and privilege assignment flaws across GraphQL APIs and custom roles.

items.title: Anthropic: That Claude Code extension compromise… couldn't be us
items.one_liner: A malicious Claude Code extension deployed via Cursor's marketplace infected thousands of developers with an information-stealing SSH backdoor.
items.summary: Anthropic has denied responsibility for a malicious update to an official Claude Code extension published on Cursor's marketplace that infected up to 5,000 developers. An unknown threat actor compromised Cursor's marketplace to distribute a tampered extension version containing a persistent SSH backdoor targeting Windows, macOS, and Linux. Although the backdoor failed to open a reverse SSH tunnel in most cases due to insufficient administrative privileges on victim machines, the payload successfully collected host system metadata and installed persistence mechanisms. Cursor temporarily shut down its extension marketplace, rotated keys, and coordinated removal of the malicious package.
items.bottom_line: Cursor users who installed the tampered Claude Code extension must hunt for dropped persistence mechanisms regardless of whether local privilege escalation succeeded.

items.title: CVE-2026-109516 (CRITICAL 9.8): The Bot for Telegram on WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Ac…
items.one_liner: Critical authentication bypass CVE-2026-109516 in WooCommerce Telegram bot plugin enables complete account takeover on WordPress sites.
items.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-109516 with a CVSS score of 9.8, affects all versions up to 1.3.0 of the 'Bot for Telegram on WooCommerce' plugin for WordPress. The unauthenticated REST endpoint performs no signature verification and allows attackers to forge bot updates specifying arbitrary usernames. The system subsequently resolves the user and creates an insecure login token that can be redeemed at an unprotected endpoint to issue persistent administrator session cookies. Consequently, unauthenticated attackers can achieve full account takeover of any registered user, including site administrators.
items.bottom_line: WordPress sites running vulnerable versions of the Bot for Telegram on WooCommerce plugin face unauthenticated remote account takeover.

items.title: CVE-2026-120338 - Prefab UI Pyodide sandbox escape to host RCE
items.one_liner: A Pyodide sandbox escape in Prefab UI allows remote code execution on host operating systems via unrestricted Deno permissions.
items.summary: CVE-2026-120338 is a sandbox escape vulnerability in Prefab UI versions 0.14.0 through 0.20.2 affecting its Generative UI sandbox running Python inside Pyodide within a Deno subprocess. The launcher starts Deno with unrestricted filesystem and network permissions while exposing the Deno API on the JavaScript global object via Pyodide's js module. Unauthenticated attackers who can supply code to FastMCP servers can execute arbitrary read and write operations on the host OS and persist execution by injecting a .pth file into site-packages. The flaw was resolved in version 0.21.0 by revoking Deno permissions before processing code.
items.bottom_line: Prefab UI versions 0.14.0 to 0.20.2 allow remote attackers with access to Generative UI endpoints to achieve host RCE via exposed Deno bindings.

items.title: CVE-2026-98432: init_on_free=1 as an additional interim mitigation
items.one_liner: The `init_on_free=1` kernel boot parameter provides an effective interim memory-zeroing defense against information disclosure risks in CVE-2026-98432 before kernel patching.
items.summary: Rui Sousa proposed enabling the `init_on_free=1` kernel boot parameter as an additional interim hardening mitigation for CVE-2026-98432, an IPv4 TCP inet_opt use-after-free vulnerability affecting systems that cannot yet apply a fixed kernel. While `init_on_free=1` does not prevent the dangling pointer dereference, it zeroes out slab objects and pages upon release, ensuring that any use-after-free read returns zeroes instead of previous memory contents. This mitigates information disclosure and complements existing packet-filter mitigations like nftables rules, at a modest performance cost of 1-5% on memory-free-heavy workloads.
items.bottom_line: Enable the `init_on_free=1` kernel boot parameter as an interim defense to zero freed memory and mitigate data exposure from CVE-2026-98432.

items.title: Critical Linux kernel flaw allows remote root attacks on MPTCP servers
items.one_liner: An AI-developed exploit for a critical Linux kernel MPTCP use-after-free vulnerability achieves unauthenticated remote root code execution.
items.summary: Anthropic security researchers have developed an exploit for CVE-2026-98432, a critical use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP networking code with a CVSS score of 9.8. The race condition occurs during connection request processing in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() and affects Linux kernels dating back to version 4.4, impacting major distributions such as Ubuntu, RHEL, and Rocky Linux. Although Red Hat initially classified the flaw as a moderate denial-of-service issue (CVSS 5.9), Anthropic demonstrated that an unreleased Claude AI model autonomously created an exploit that bypassed KASLR and achieved remote root code execution within 53 minutes on servers running Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners. Go language runtimes since version 1.24 enable MPTCP by default for TCP listeners, potentially exposing services without administrator awareness.

items.bottom_line: Linux administrators must immediately patch CVE-2026-98432 across affected kernel versions to mitigate AI-verified remote root exploits targeting MPTCP listeners.

items.one_liner: Apache MINA 3.0 users face an unpatchable RCE vulnerability and must downgrade to the 2.2.X branch to remain secure.
items.summary: Apache MINA 3.0.0 through 3.0.0-M2 contains a critical unsafe deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2026-118636) in the JavaNativeMessageDecoder component. items.bottom_line: If your application uses Apache MINA 3.0.0-M2 or earlier, you are vulnerable to RCE and must migrate to the 2.2.X branch immediately.

items.one_liner: An unauthenticated file write and fastcgi execution vulnerability in NUUO Crystal Server allows remote attackers to achieve root-level code execution.
items.summary: Researchers have publicly disclosed a critical 9.8-rated unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in NUUO Crystal Server version 3.19.0.85, an Ubuntu-based video management and NVR appliance. The flaw stems from an unauthenticated upload script (upload.php) that accepts arbitrary client-supplied filenames and passes them directly to the copy() function without session validation, extension checks, or path restrictions. An anonymous remote attacker can post a multipart PHP payload directly into the served web root (/NU20/web/) and subsequently trigger execution through the server's FastCGI mapping. This enables unauthenticated command execution as the web service account without requiring credentials or memory corruption primitives.
key_facts: Vulnerability Type: Unauthenticated file upload and execution (CWE-306, CWE-434, CWE-73)

items.title: NetamLoader Malware Targets Government Windows 10 Systems in Asia via .NET Injection
items.one_liner: A sophisticated supply chain attack utilizes AppDomainManager .NET injection to deploy the NetamLoader framework against government Windows systems in Asia.
items.summary: Kaspersky researchers have discovered NetamLoader, a previously undocumented .NET assembly-loading framework targeting a custom Windows 10 build used exclusively by government entities in Asia. The malware was delivered via a Windows cabinet archive placed inside the SoftwareDistribution download directory, pointing to a likely supply chain compromise of a trusted third-party vendor. Once executed, the loader processes multiple encrypted layers of XAML and JSON payloads to deploy command-and-control modules while bypassing the Antimalware Scan Interface.

items.title: Appraisal by AI: Model-driven victim prioritization in the VOLTA infostealer
items.one_liner: The VOLTA Windows infostealer uses LLMs and multi-model failover chains to automatically appraise and prioritize stolen victim assets.
items.summary: Researchers have identified VOLTA, a mature Windows infostealer that incorporates an automated AI-integration layer to perform victim-profiling and monetization triage. After harvesting credentials, browser cookies, and cryptocurrency wallets from a compromised machine, VOLTA extracts contextual data—such as home addresses, employer domains, and food delivery histories—to construct a structured dossier. This evidence bundle is transmitted via OpenRouter to an LLM system prompt instructing the model to act as a forensic intelligence analyst ranking the victim's assets by monetization value. To circumvent model safety guardrails and refusal filters, VOLTA implements a deterministic, multi-model failover chain featuring Claude, Kimi, and Gemini.
items.bottom_line: Expect cybercriminals to increasingly weaponize LLMs for automated data triage and financial valuation of compromised corporate endpoints.

items.title: State of Post-Quantum Cryptography implementations
items.one_liner: A deep dive into PQC and NIST-standardized KEM implementations highlights the urgency of moving away from quantum-vulnerable algorithms.
items.summary: Quarkslab published an overview of Post-Quantum Cryptography implementations stemming from a differential fuzzing internship project targeting open-source cryptographic libraries. The review highlights the imminent threat of 'Harvest now, decrypt later,' where adversaries store classical encrypted data to break it once quantum computers mature via Shor's algorithm. To combat this, the US NIST standardized algorithms like ML-KEM under FIPS 203, shifting traditional key exchanges to Key Encapsulation Mechanisms based on lattice problems. Major tech companies and agencies have established migration timelines targeting full post-quantum replacement before the end of the decade.
items.bottom_line: Post-quantum cryptography migration timelines are accelerating as libraries implement lattice-based KEMs to thwart 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks.

items.summary: A vulnerability in Apache Wicket's AbstractFileUploadResource allows attackers to bypass configured upload limits, leading to potential resource exhaustion. Because the resource is a singleton that relies on client-provided request parameters for size limits, an attacker can supply arbitrary values to override application-defined constraints. This allows for excessive disk or heap consumption through repeated requests. Users should upgrade to version 9.25.0 or 10.12.0 to ensure upload limits are correctly enforced.
items.bottom_line: Applications using Apache Wicket's standalone file upload resource are vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks because they fail to enforce server-side upload limits.

items.title: Google::Auth for Perl (2 CVEs)
items.one_liner: Google::Auth for Perl is vulnerable to SSRF and OAuth state hijacking, impacting local authentication security.
items.summary: Two security vulnerabilities have been identified in the Google::Auth Perl library. CVE-2026-74759 allows Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via unvalidated credential_source URLs in AWS external account configurations. CVE-2026-74760 allows a local attacker to hijack authentication by exploiting a failure to validate the OAuth state parameter in the gcloud-auth login callback. Users are advised to upgrade to future releases or use the --no-browser flag as a workaround for the authentication issue.
key_facts: CVE-2026-74759: SSRF in AWS external account credentials
items.bottom_line: Perl developers using Google::Auth must be aware that their local authentication flow can be intercepted by malicious local processes until they upgrade.

items.title: Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent
items.one_liner: German cost-of-living protests turned violent across multiple cities, leading to extensive police deployments and arrests.
items.summary: Protests organized by the group Gen Z regelt in Germany against underfunding, high living costs, and military service turned violent in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne, and Hamburg. Demonstrators threw fireworks, stones, and bottles at emergency services, prompting police to deploy water cannons and special units. Officials reported numerous arrests and injuries, including 27 police officers in Berlin and 120 arrests in Hamburg, with interior ministers blaming left-wing extremist infiltration. The unrest mirrors recent mass protests in France and has drawn calls from officials for harsh punishments.

items.title: India's opposition holds mega rally seeking election chief's resignation
items.one_liner: India's opposition held a massive protest in Delhi demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over voter list revisions.
items.summary: Tens of thousands of protesters gathered at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan for a mega rally organized by the opposition INDIA bloc to demand the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar. The protests target a controversial Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls that removed over 130 million names, which opposition parties claim is a systematic attempt to disenfranchise eligible voters in favor of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party. While opposition leaders like Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge accused the poll panel of destroying democracy, the BJP dismissed the gathering as a calculated conspiracy to incite anarchy and instability.
items.bottom_line: The INDIA bloc staged a major protest against India's Election Commission over electoral roll revisions, intensifying political friction ahead of elections.

items.title: CVE-2026-115946: XS::ibbrotli versions before 1.2.1.0 for Perl bundle a brotli library with an out-of-bounds write in the decoder
items.one_liner: Perl's XS::libbrotli module is vulnerable to an out-of-bounds write due to a bundled, outdated Brotli library.
items.summary: A security vulnerability, CVE-2026-115946, has been discovered in XS::libbrotli versions prior to 1.2.1.0, which bundles a vulnerable version of the Brotli library. The issue involves an out-of-bounds write in the decoder, which can be triggered when decompressing untrusted data, potentially leading to memory disclosure, process crashes, or arbitrary code execution. Users are urged to upgrade to version 1.2.1.0 and reinstall all dependent XS modules to ensure the fix is applied, as updating the system-level Brotli library does not resolve the issue for bundled copies.
key_facts: CWE-1395: Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component
items.bottom_line: Developers using XS::libbrotli must upgrade to version 1.2.1.0 and rebuild dependent modules to mitigate the risk of arbitrary code execution.

items.title: CVE-2026-120189 - D-Link DIR-505 TFTP Upload Filename tftpd mp_upload_file stack-based overflow
items.one_liner: D-Link DIR-505 version 1.10B02 is vulnerable to a remote stack-based buffer overflow in its TFTP upload handler.
items.summary: A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-120189, has been identified in version 1.10B02 of the D-Link DIR-505 router. The flaw resides in the save_upload_file and mp_upload_file functions within the /usr/bin/tftpd component's TFTP Upload Filename Handler. Remote attackers can exploit this vulnerability by manipulating the upload filename to trigger arbitrary code execution or a denial of service. Publicly available exploits for this issue increase the risk to exposed consumer and small-business devices.
items.bottom_line: Isolate or replace legacy D-Link DIR-505 devices exposed to the internet to prevent remote exploitation of this TFTP overflow.

items.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials
items.one_liner: A US judge blocked the Trump administration from threatening election officials over ballot processing ahead of midterm elections.
items.summary: A federal judge has issued an order barring the Trump administration and Department of Justice from threatening local and state election officials with criminal prosecution over ballot processing. The ruling specifically blocks authorities from forcing election workers to set aside 20,000 ballots in California that the administration alleged belonged to non-citizens. The court found that federal demands and armed Department of Homeland Security visits would severely disrupt election administration and unlawfully disenfranchise registered voters. The legal intervention comes immediately ahead of midterm elections that will determine control of the US Congress.
items.bottom_line: Federal courts have halted DOJ and DHS efforts to penalize local election workers over disputed non-citizen voter ballots.

items.title: Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe
items.one_liner: Mass protests over cost-of-living issues in France led to hundreds of arrests as unrest spreads across European nations.
items.summary: Hundreds of thousands of protesters demonstrated across France during nationwide rallies against the rising cost of living and poor public services, leading to clashes with police in Paris. French authorities deployed heavy security, resulting in at least 290 arrests and the use of tear gas by police in Paris where roughly 70,000 people demonstrated. The protests precede an upcoming general strike organized across the country. Similar demonstrations by youth and citizens have also broken out in Albania, Germany, and Italy.

items.one_liner: A humanitarian ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump enabled hundreds of Ukrainian residents to evacuate the front-line, Russian-occupied city of Oleshky after years of severe deprivation.
items.summary: Hundreds of residents from the Russian-occupied front-line city of Oleshky in Ukraine evacuated via Belarus after enduring years of intense shelling, mined escape routes, and extreme shortages of food and supplies. The evacuations were enabled by a four-hour humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump in the Kherson region. Up to 6,000 people had been estimated to remain in the area prior to the convoy of 25 buses arriving to transport evacuees. Upon reaching Chernihiv in northern Ukraine, families experienced emotional reunions while facing ongoing challenges regarding displacement and where to relocate next.

items.title: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
items.one_liner: DR Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak crosses 5,000 deaths across eight provinces amidst violent community resistance.
items.summary: An ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths, making it the country's deadliest in history. The epidemic has affected eight of 26 provinces with over 10,300 confirmed cases and a case fatality rate of 48.6%, driven by the Bundibugyo species for which no specific treatment or vaccine currently exists. The epicenter remains in the conflict-ridden Ituri province, complicating containment efforts and sparking violent community resistance against healthcare workers and politicians. While limited cases have been reported in Kenya, Uganda, and Nigeria, the World Health Organization is scaling up control measures and vaccine clinical trials to halt transmission.
items.bottom_line: The deadliest Ebola outbreak in DR Congo's history has killed over 5,000 people while armed conflict and local mistrust hinder containment.

items.title: Spain train disaster clouds Sánchez chances of re-election
items.one_liner: A fatal high-speed train collision in central Spain kills 69 people, triggering a political crisis for Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez ahead of elections.
items.summary: A fatal train collision on the high-speed rail line south of Madrid in central Spain has resulted in 69 confirmed deaths, triggering a major national disaster just weeks before a snap general election. Transport Minister Oscar Puente defended the LZB signalling safety system despite it failing 170 times this year, instead attributing the crash to severe human error by a controller who cleared a stalled train to move while another was stopped ahead. The disaster has severely damaged public confidence in the Socialist-led government of Pedro Sánchez, with the opposition People's Party demanding the minister's resignation.

items.title: CVE-2026-120135: Apache Thrift: Java TProtocolUtil.skip() does not limit the recursion depth by default
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-120135 introduces an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in Apache Thrift Java TProtocolUtil.skip().
items.summary: Apache Thrift Java bindings prior to version 0.24.0 contain an uncontrolled recursion vulnerability in the TProtocolUtil.skip() method. The method fails to limit recursion depth by default when parsing nested data structures, allowing an attacker to trigger a stack overflow and cause a denial of service. The vulnerability carries a CVSS 4.0 score of 8.2 and is fixed in version 0.24.0.
items.bottom_line: Java applications utilizing Apache Thrift must upgrade to library version 0.24.0 to mitigate potential denial-of-service attacks.

items.title: Re: CVE-2026-102508: Apache PLC4X: OPC UA secure channel: integrity bypass, unverifiable server certificate, and silent downgrade
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-102508 in Apache PLC4X combines an integrity check bypass, unverified server certificates, and silent policy downgrades.
items.summary: Apache PLC4X client library versions 0.9.0 through 0.13.1 suffer from multiple security flaws in the OPC UA secure channel handling, tracked as CVE-2026-102508. Vulnerabilities include an inverted signature verification check combined with a message length mismatch that causes invalid cryptographic signatures to be accepted. Additionally, default settings use permissive server certificate verification and permit silent security policy downgrades to 'None'. An on-path attacker or malicious server can exploit these flaws to bypass integrity checks and intercept secure sessions. PLC4X version 1.0.0 addresses these issues.
items.bottom_line: Industrial systems utilizing Apache PLC4X client libraries must upgrade to version 1.0.0 to prevent OPC UA channel interception and integrity bypasses.

items.title: CVE-2026-73322: Apache Pinot: Incorrect authorization in the single-stage query engine allows reading unauthorized dimension tables via lookup()
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-73322 allows authenticated users to query unauthorized dimension tables via lookup() in Apache Pinot's single-stage query engine.
items.summary: Apache Pinot versions through 1.5.1 contain an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the single-stage query engine. When broker access control is enabled, the single-stage engine authorizes only the table named in the FROM clause, failing to validate dimension tables referenced via the lookup() transform function. Authenticated users authorized for any table can read columns and arbitrary rows from unauthorized dimension tables, bypassing row-level security filters. The multi-stage query engine is unaffected, and users should upgrade to version 1.6.0 or later.
items.bottom_line: Apache Pinot deployments using the single-stage query engine must upgrade to version 1.6.0 to prevent unauthorized access to dimension tables.

items.title: CVE-2026-13575: HTTP::Session versions before 0.54 for Perl allow memcached command injection via unfiltered session ids in HTTP::Session::Store::CHI
items.one_liner: Perl's HTTP::Session module is vulnerable to memcached command injection due to insufficient filtering of session IDs.
items.summary: A security vulnerability, CVE-2026-13575, has been identified in Perl's HTTP::Session module versions prior to 0.54. The flaw allows for memcached command injection because the module fails to filter session IDs before passing them to the CHI cache store. An attacker can inject CR and LF characters into the session ID, causing the memcached server to interpret subsequent bytes as additional commands. Users are advised to upgrade to version 0.54 or later to remediate the issue.
key_facts: CWE-93: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences
items.bottom_line: Developers using HTTP::Session for Perl must upgrade to version 0.54 immediately to prevent potential command injection attacks.

items.title: ElectroNG is now open source!

items.summary: Doyensec has open-sourced both its Electron static application security testing desktop application and its core analysis engine under the Apache License 2.0. items.title: GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise
items.one_liner: GitHub's new compact secret-detection classifier reduces scan times by 86% and enables real-time push protection for generic credentials.
items.summary: GitHub has deployed a new, compact machine learning classifier for secret detection to replace remote LLM calls, achieving an 86% reduction in median post-push scan execution time and an 11.5% higher owner-weighted alert precision. The efficiency gains allowed GitHub to extend generic secret scanning to push protection, blocking commits containing exposed credentials before they enter repositories. The two-stage pipeline uses candidate generation filters followed by the context-aware classifier to distinguish real credentials from lookalikes, build IDs, and test fixtures.
key_facts: Scan Speed Improvement: 86% lower median scan execution time
items.bottom_line: Replacing remote LLM calls with a specialized compact classifier enables fast, accurate secret detection at scale during push protection.

items.title: Democrat endorses Republican candidate in key Michigan Senate race as party spat erupts

items.title: Char Dham helicopter operators threaten to halt services over DGCA's two-pilot rule
items.one_liner: A new two-pilot mandate for Uttarakhand helicopter operations is triggering a service strike due to concerns over financial viability and ignored safety hazards.
items.summary: Char Dham helicopter operators have threatened to suspend services starting November 2, 2026, in response to a new DGCA mandate requiring two pilots for every charter sortie. The regulation was implemented following a fatal helicopter crash in Joshimath on October 30 that killed six people. Operators argue the requirement is financially unsustainable and claim authorities are scapegoating them while ignoring persistent safety hazards like drone and paragliding activity near flight paths. UCADA officials maintain that drone risks are being investigated and that specific flight routes have been established to mitigate these dangers.
items.bottom_line: Helicopter services for the Char Dham pilgrimage are set to halt on November 2 unless regulators and operators reach a compromise on the new two-pilot mandate.

items.title: Carlyle, KKR Get Ready to Snatch Up Bargain Loans
items.one_liner: Private equity giants like Carlyle and KKR are setting up credit lines to buy discounted US leveraged loans for CLOs.

items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape.
